kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-02.title: Count factors 2 and 5
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-02.body:
Each zero at the end needs one factor $10 = 2 \times 5$.

- $201325 = 25 \times 8053$, and 8053 is not divisible by 5: two factors 5, no factor 2.
- $201326 = 2 \times 100663$, and 100663 is odd: one factor 2, no factor 5.
- $201317$ is odd and does not end in 0 or 5: no factor 2 or 5.

The product has $2^1$ and $5^2$, so only one factor 10.

**Answer: (B) 1**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-11.title: Bands times sectors
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-11.body:
A meridian is a half circle from the North Pole to the South Pole. 10 meridians cut the globe like an orange into 10 slices.

A parallel is a circle around the globe at a fixed latitude. 10 parallels cut the globe into 11 horizontal bands.

Each band is cut by the meridians into 10 pieces: $11 \times 10 = 110$ areas.

**Answer: (D) 110**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-11.title: Add one line at a time
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-11.body:
With the 10 meridians only, there are 10 areas. Each new parallel crosses all 10 slices and splits each into two, adding 10 areas. After 10 parallels: $10 + 10 \times 10 = 110$.

**Answer: (D) 110**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-19.title: Descendants form a square
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-19.body:
Let Francois have $n$ children. Each child has $n - 1$ siblings, so each child has $n - 1$ children of their own. There are no great-grandchildren.

Descendants: $n + n(n-1) = n^2$.

His age is a perfect square between 60 and 80 (he has had his 60th birthday but not yet his 80th): only $64 = 8^2$.

**Answer: (B) 64**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-19.title: Test the choices
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-19.body:
The number of descendants $n + n(n-1) = n^2$ must be a perfect square. Among 62, 64, 67, 70, 72 only 64 is a square (8 children, each with 7 children: $8 + 56 = 64$).

**Answer: (B) 64**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-21.title: Column by column
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-21.body:
Two 4-digit numbers add to a 5-digit number, so $A = 1$.

- **Units:** $E + E$ ends in $E$, so $E = 0$ (no carry).
- **Thousands:** $B + B$ (+ carry) gives the 2-digit "$AE$" $= 10$. So $2B + c = 10$ with carry $c \in \{0,1\}$; $2B = 9$ is impossible, so $c = 0$ and $B = 5$.
- **Tens:** $C + A = C + 1$ must end in $B = 5$, so $C = 4$ (no carry).
- **Hundreds:** $D + D = C = 4$ with no carry (consistent with $c = 0$), so $D = 2$.

Check: $5240 + 5210 = 10450$ ✓ ($A=1, E=0, C=4, B=5$).

**Answer: (A) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-23.title: Small example
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-23.body:
Replace 2013 by 2: up to $2^6 = 64$ there are $S = 8$ squares ($1,4,\dots,64$) and $Q = 4$ cubes ($1, 8, 27, 64$). Then $S = 2Q$, which matches the pattern $S = 2013Q$ with 2013 replaced by 2, and none of the other relations holds ($S^3 = 512 \ne Q^2 = 16$).

**Answer: (D) $S = 2013Q$**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-27.title: Count singer-songs
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-27.body:
Every song has 3 singers, so (total of everyone's song counts) $= 3 \times$ (number of songs).

Nick and Simon each sang more than 5 and fewer than 8 songs (James sang the most), so each sang 6 or 7. The total is $8 + 5 + (6 \text{ or } 7) + (6 \text{ or } 7)$, i.e. 25, 26 or 27. Only 27 is divisible by 3.

So there were $27 \div 3 = 9$ songs.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-27.title: Count the guitar instead
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-27.body:
In each song exactly one member plays guitar. With $T$ songs, a member who sang $s$ songs played guitar $T - s$ times, and these add up to $T$:

$(T - 8) + (T - 5) + (T - n) + (T - s) = T$, so $3T = 13 + n + s$ with $n, s \in \{6, 7\}$. Only $n = s = 7$ gives a multiple of 3: $3T = 27$, $T = 9$.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-30.title: Divisors come in pairs
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0708-30.body:
If $1 < a < b < c$ are the three smallest divisors of $N$ greater than 1, then the three greatest divisors below $N$ are $\frac Na, \frac Nb, \frac Nc$. The condition is

$$\frac Na + \frac Nb + \frac Nc > N \iff \frac1a + \frac1b + \frac1c > 1.$$

- If $a \ge 3$, then $\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c \le \frac13+\frac14+\frac15 < 1$. So $a = 2$.
- Then we need $\frac1b + \frac1c > \frac12$. If $b \ge 4$, $\frac1b + \frac1c \le \frac14 + \frac15 < \frac12$. So $b = 3$.

Hence $N$ is divisible by 2 and 3, i.e. by 6. Such $N$ exist, e.g. $N = 12$: $6 + 4 + 3 = 13 > 12$.

Counterexamples to the other options: 6 itself fails (divisors below 6 are only 3, 2, 1, sum 6), but 12 works and is not divisible by 5 or 7; $N = 30$ ($15 + 10 + 6 = 31 > 30$) is not divisible by 4.

**Answer: (C)**
